prompt: Here's the OAuth "find-or-create" method our auth service runs on every social sign-in (Google/GitHub) — given the incoming profile (provider id, email, name, picture, locale) it looks the user up first by provider id, then by email if that misses, and always writes the row before returning `{ user, isNewUser }`. In production this traffic is dominated by returning, already-linked users, so this hot path is paying for two sequential reads plus a wasted write on every single login. Optimize the returning-user path down to a single read and zero writes without changing any identity-linking behavior: a first-time login must still insert and report `isNewUser: true`, an existing email-only account must still get the provider linked and converge to one row, and a returning user must resolve to the same row with `isNewUser: false`. Walk me through your approach before showing the fix.
